selections.comment: Lead Artist was tenacious when he shaded victory over Dancing Gemini in the Lockinge at Newbury and there is very little to choose between these two high-class individuals as they gear up for what promises to be another thrilling encounter. However, ROSALLION's third-placed finish that day was a very encouraging effort. That was his first start since he sealed victory with a lightning burst of speed in the St James's Palace here 12 months ago and he merits the utmost respect once again. Notable Speech, who was fourth in the Lockinge, and the now Australian-trained Carl Spackler add further depth to a splendid curtain raiser.

selections.comment: A strong renewal where the form of the Lockinge Stakes may be reversed by a couple who finished in behind Lead Artist who got first run on the field that day. It's much more difficult to race close to the pace and win over this C&D but it may not be his closest rival that day Dancing Gemini who is the beneficiary given he had a big fitness edge last time. 2024 Guineas winner NOTABLE SPEECH and Rosallion were behind that pair at Newbury but they both hadn’t had a run this year previously and the latter hadn't been seen since landing the St James's Palace over C&D at this meeting last summer. There was only a neck between them that day and they got the better of each other once last year so should be closely matched once again. Small preference is for the Godolphin horse who hasn't the injury issues of his rival and who showed a liking for fast ground in the Sussex Stakes and Breeders' Cup. Of the others Sardinian Warrior is still on the upgrade and as a C&D winner will appreciate the drop back in trip having been outstayed by a classy rival in the Prix D'Ispahan last time. He can compete for a place behind the front pair.

selections.comment: Aidan O'Brien has won this 10 times and has strong claims of improving that record with Warsaw and GSTAAD. The former wasn't fancied for debut but overcame a slow start to win over a stiff 5f turning over an odds on shot while posting a good speed figure and should appreciate the longer trip here. However Ryan Moore has opted for the former after he turned over a well touted stablemate on debut also relishing the stiff finish. The pair that day came a long way clear of the remainder suggesting that they were a class apart and the selection could take this step up in grade in his stride. Andab wasn't beaten far last time by a top class stablemate of the selection and could make it a 1-2-3 for Ireland with his experience edge a bonus. Of the home challenge course winner Military Code is feared most with his form working out extremely well. He's bred to appreciate this extra distance and has posted big speed figures on both of his runs so far.

selections.comment: Asfoora took this contest in 2024 appreciating the stiff track at the trip and has proved she retains her ability this term with a Group victory in Australia. However, she massively showed the benefit of a prep run on these shores last year and the lack of it this time is a big concern. Both Regional and BELIEVING were not beaten far behind here and have the potential to reverse that form here. Both are strong stayers at the trip so will appreciate the likely fast pace with plenty of it drawn around the latter which should give her a nice tow into the race. If getting it she can pounce late and follow up on his deserved Group 1 victory in the Al Quoz last time. Though drawn on the other side away from most of the pace Starlust is another who is likely to be flying home at the finish and the Breeders' Cup winner holds solid each way claims on favourable fast ground.

selections.comment: The UK, Irish and French Guineas winners all collide in what promises to be a great spectacle. Ruling Court got the better of FIELD OF GOLD at Newmarket but he got first run that day as the runner up was given a poor ride which the jockey paid the price for. However he made amends at the Curragh in impressive fashion producing a big speed figure and being eased at the finish so is fancied to reverse that form if ridden closer to that re-opposing rival. Henri Matisse was given a fine ride at Longchamp getting up late as the runner up possibly kicked on a bit early. He is open to further progression and the faster ground won't be an issue given he was a Breeders' Cup winner on firm late last year so he is very much respected.

selections.comment: The Irish hold a particularly strong hand here notably the stables of Willie Mullins and Joseph O'Brien. Poniros and Reaching High both go for the former and are unexposed on the flat for the stable. The first of those went off favourite for the Cambridgeshire when last seen on the flat but was ultimately well held. However he landed the Triumph Hurdle this spring on stable debut so likely has more to offer on the flat over staying trips. His stablemate was well fancied for his stable debut and looked the winner everywhere but the line so holds fair claims with improvement likely from that first run in nearly a year. It is 2024 Galway Hurdle winner NURBURGRING who appeals most though having had a sharpener on the flat over an inadequate 10f. Prior to that he ran a big race behind a future Grade 1 winner in a hot Cheltenham handicap and he also ran well in the Irish Cesarewitch last autumn despite a troubled passage. If ridden more positively in this discipline he will likely improve and should go close. His progressive stablemate Leinster is also feared having gone off too quickly in the Chester Cup last time.

If ridden more positively in this discipline he will likely improve and should go close. His progressive stablemate Leinster is also feared having gone off too quickly in the Chester Cup last time.

He does have his stamina to prove over this longer trip but that victory here last year is worth marking up significantly as he fared much the best of those ridden close to the pace. He will provide a big challenge along with Haunted Dream who placed in this last year and ran well behind a top class rival in Saudi Arabia last time. He has a small break to overcome but should run his race while last year's unlucky Hampton Court loser King's Gambit also rates a threat. He didn't take to the blinkers last time when a big drifter suggesting that he was in need of the run and could bounce back at a track he likes.

selections.comment: An extremely open race to close the card where dual purpose performers may be the way to go. JESSE EVANS has run very well in a couple of renewals of the Galway Hurdle and proved he retained his ability with an easy chase win last time. He wasn't knocked about from a poor position on his sole flat start this year and looks potentially thrown in back in a handicap on favourable quick ground. He could get the better of Lavender Hill Mob who was a game winner last time in a race which threw up a next time out winner. He was too keen over this C&D in the Queen's Vase last year but remains unexposed over staying trips and will pose a big threat. Charlus represents the top jumps yard around which has a good record at this meeting and though he was outclassed in the Triumph Hurdle last time he likely has more to offer in this sphere having placed at Listed level when trained in France. The unexposed French Master completes the list of dangers as he was worth more than the winning margin last time when not given the best ride on his first attempt over this trip. The first time blinkers could deliver further improvement.

He will no doubt be a well-fancied runner in the market, so most will expect him to land this contest. Command The Stars ran well on racecourse debut when coming 5th out of eight runners at Haydock; he will no doubt put that experience to good use here. selections.comment: ORIGINAL OUTLAW hails from a powerful yard who probably don't normally persist this long with a horse who won't win, so that could speak for something here, as they probably see this as a winning opportunity for him. His last three runs have been in handicap company; therefore, he steps back into maiden company here, and given the fact he is rated 82, that is a fairly high benchmark for the others to hit given their lack of racecourse experience. Comanche Warrior was only beaten by half a legnth on racecourse debut at Carlisle last time out, and given the connections, it is expected that he will come on for the run here. Forest Caper also came third on racecourse debut last time, which was a good enough effort to suggest there could be more improvement to come from him; therefore, he can run well and place here.

He is in good form at present, and the yard are also going very well at present; therefore, Dumfries looks primed to strike again here. Sunny Orange was a decent 2nd last time out, and he arrives into this race off the same mark as last time; therefore, he can go well again. And although Kalganov has not won in a year and a half and is 20 lb lower than his last winning mark, that could mean he is well handicapped and will be sure to go well again here.

It is clear to see he is not running at his peak at present given the fact he has dropped down to a mark of 72 here; however, the 2nd placed effort from last time out would suggest there is still a bit of a fire in his belly here. If he can reproduce the effort from last time out, then he will be hard to stop here. Kitsune Power is trained by someone who does very well at this track, and a bit like Lincoln Rockstar, this horse came 2nd last time out; therefore, they will look to build from that effort. Freddy Robinson has been running consistently recently, and he can go in and place once again.

When winning for the first time, he escapes the penalty here and is sure to get a pretty big hike up in the weights when he eventually gets assessed by the handicapper. The change of tactics and headgear last time worked wonders for him, and if he is in the same vein of form here, he will be hard to peg back. Inspiring Speeches is yet to win in his career but has looked like knocking on the door, and he can build on that 4th-placed effort from last time and go a few places better here. Daring Leader ran a decent 3rd on debut at this venue for the stable debut; he can build on that and run another good race here.

He was just touched off seeking the double last time back at 1m and arrives in rude health and should be a real handful if seeing out the trip

Spirit Of Jenny, a fine second on debut despite being sent off a 40/1 outsider in an 8-runner event, and Your Love, a good 3rd last time on Wolverhampton's Tapeta surface, are the principal dangers of those with epxerience and are likely to be in the shake-up. Of the newcomers, Portoken is most interesting. A daughter of Goken, a Group 3 winner at 5f as a 2yo, out of a dam with smart form at two (placed at Listed level), she could go well on debut and could play a part. The market can guide but those with experience look likey to dominate

The market can guide but those with experience look likey to dominate

Wiltshire Lad needs to bounce back after a couple of moderate efforts on turf this term but won over course and distance on final start last year on nursery handicap debut and is a danger to all if rediscovering similar levels

ROYAL FIXATION as the most expensive purchase (180,000gns) makes most appeal, buy Palace Pier with plenty more speed in the pedigree should take all the beating. Mandarin Spirit is another to consider, the yard won this last year and 2022 with Alice Fairfax and Glenlaurel. Loma Express looks an interesting contender too, particularly given the James Ferguson yard are in terrific form and should be another with plenty of speed.
